rubric: Every field has a visible label that stays on screen, not a placeholder standing in for a label.
Each error message sits next to the field it belongs to, says in plain words what to fix, and does not rely on colour alone.
What the person already typed is kept, and the password requirements are visible without having to fail first.
The form is a single clear column with one primary button and a sensible order and grouping of fields.
Inputs are easy to see and use: visible borders, comfortable height and legible text size.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A shows the whole page, including the terms checkbox and its error, the one primary button and the login link. Every error has an icon and a plain fix right below its field, and the password rule shows without having to fail first. B's error details are a bit stronger: the password rule sits above the field, errors start with 'Error:', there's a Show toggle, and it says 'Yours has 7'. But the screenshot is cut off before the terms checkbox and the submit button, so I couldn't check its layout and button, which costs it on item 4. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A's screenshot is cut off after the household-size field, so its terms checkbox, terms error and primary button never appear, even though the request was to see how the errors look. What A does show is strong: the password requirements sit above the field, and each error has an icon, an 'Error:' prefix and very specific wording. B shows the complete form in one clean column, with errors next to each field, an icon and plain wording. Its password hint is small and sits below the input, but it is visible before any failure.
